global_principles: Center African perspectives and lived experiences
Balance warmth and professionalism; avoid NGO pity language
Be specific about places, people, and impact, not vague generalities
Use clear, accessible English; avoid heavy jargon

tones.name: EditorialFeature
tones.description: Narrative, reflective, rooted in reporting and lived experience.
useCases: Landing sections highlighting creators or projects
do: Use vivid but grounded description of scenes and people
Highlight agency of African subjects, not just challenges

tones.name: PlatformVoice
tones.description: Clear, confident product voice used in UI copy and system messages.
do: Explain why something matters in one short phrase
Reflect pride in African creativity and innovation
dont: Use slang that might not travel across regions

tones.name: FundingAppeal
tones.description: Impact-focused but respectful; connects support to concrete outcomes.
do: Explain how support unlocks more African stories, projects, or tools
dont: Use shame or guilt to drive action

structure: Optional second line connecting support to outcomes

good: Help more African filmmakers share their work.
Your support keeps this reporting independent.
bad: Donate or this work cannot continue.

structure: Friendly acknowledgement of the empty state

good: No supporters yet. Be the first to back this project.
No stories here yet. Explore other creators while we curate this space.

fr: Prefer simple, clear phrasing over literal translation.
Maintain respectful but warm tone; avoid overly formal bureaucratic language.

lintingRules: Disallow phrases from tones[*].dont lists in UI copy
Enforce maxChars from content_patterns where applicable
